gotchas.topic: institution money totals exclude football and basketball
gotchas.note: In the institutions table, il_revenue_*, il_expense_*, il_total_rev*, il_total_exp* and il_total_revenue_all / il_total_expense_all cover ALL SPORTS EXCEPT FOOTBALL AND BASKETBALL, even though the codebook labels them 'Total ... per Team'. They equal the sum of the sports rows minus Football and Basketball for every school-year. For a school's full men's or women's spending, sum the sports table or use v_spending_by_gender. (il_*partic* and il_*opexp* columns are full totals.)

Much athletics spending isn't assigned to any team (facilities, administration, some staff): tot_expense_all_notalloc. Sum of team expenses + not-allocated = grand_total_expense. Men's vs. women's comparisons cover team expenses only; say so, and give the unallocated amount when it matters.

Sport-level participation counts an athlete once per team, so an athlete on three teams counts three times (sum_partic_*, il_sum_partic_*). For institution-wide shares (proportionality) and per-athlete figures, use the unduplicated counts undup_ct_partic_men / undup_ct_partic_women, as v_proportionality does.

Co-ed team participants are reported separately (partic_coed_men / partic_coed_women; rev_coed_*, exp_coed_*). Columns ending in _menall / _womenall and sum_partic_* INCLUDE co-ed members of that sex; partic_men / exp_men etc. do not. The unduplicated counts include co-ed members. Say whether a figure includes co-ed teams.

Not a column. Use the view v_proportionality: female share of full-time undergraduates minus female share of (unduplicated) athletes, in percentage points. A positive gap means women are underrepresented among athletes. This is prong 1 of the three-part test only; it does not establish compliance or non-compliance.

efmalecount / effemalecount / eftotalcount are full-time undergraduates (the population EADA reports under 20 U.S.C. 1092(g); codebook labels are just 'Total Men' / 'Total Women' / 'Grand Total'). eftotalcount = efmalecount + effemalecount in every row. Not total enrollment.

Names are official IPEDS names (e.g. 'University of California-Berkeley', 'The University of Alabama'). Resolve user wording through the institution_aliases table before filtering; filter on unitid afterwards.

survey_year is the END of the academic year: 2025 means 2024-25 (the Department of Education's own label for the file). Loaded: 2016-2025 (2015-16 to 2024-25). 2021 (2020-21) is the COVID year with ~200 fewer schools reporting; don't call a 2020-to-2021 drop a trend. EADA trails real time, so the latest year predates revenue sharing (2025-26).

Revenue and expense columns are separate. About 61% of school-years report grand total revenue exactly equal to expenses (institutional support fills the gap), so revenue minus expenses is NOT a measure of profit. opexp* columns are game-day operating expenses only, a subset of total expenses (exp_*, expense_*); per-participant and per-team opexp columns are averages, not totals.

The sports table has only sponsored sports: rows with no participants were dropped at build time (the 2019-20 file listed unsponsored sports with zeros; other years never did). So a missing school+sport row means the sport isn't sponsored. Within a row, partic_men / exp_men / rev_men (and the women's equivalents) are NULL when that sport has no team of that sex; the _menall / _womenall and sum_ columns are 0 instead.

Use the sports column (text) to filter, after get_enum_values. Track and swimming are reported either combined ('Track and Field and Cross Country (combined)', 'Swimming and Diving (combined)') or split, depending on the school; count both forms. 'Other Sports' lumps unlisted sports.

EADA has no conference column. classification_name gives the division (e.g. 'NCAA Division I-FBS', 'NCAA Division III with football', 'NJCAA Division I'). Some values have trailing spaces; use TRIM or ILIKE.

EADA records institutional athletics spending. Third-party NIL deals never appear here, and revenue-sharing payments are not in the years loaded. Use the nil_facts table for NIL figures and say which money flow each number belongs to.
